summary:
DSA-on-branches has three known failures. Each is fixable, but the fixes concatenate into a different design called **hierarchical Zone B collapse**.

**FM-5 (eviction destroyed context)**: When the selector actually evicted a branch, the run failed—the branch vanished entirely. This is fixable by not deleting, only summarizing. The evicted branch stays in the store (L1/L2); eviction writes a one-line tombstone with a `context_fetch` pointer ("`auth-refactor` collapsed; see node n14"). The infrastructure already exists (§8's rehydration metadata); it was never wired into the eviction path.

**FM-8 (cache-safe selector proved inert)**: To avoid breaking the byte-prefix cache, the selector had to be pass-through every turn (the monotone lock-in). That's not a property of selection itself—it's the price of trying to select *per turn* without rewriting the prefix, which violates the volatile-bit law. The fix is to select at rare, scheduled epochs instead: when Zone B exceeds a budget (say 100+ branches), the system runs one LLM-driven selection pass, rewrites Zone B with a super-summary, absorbs one cache epoch (1.25×), then freezes again. The 0.1× re-read savings on all subsequent turns amortize that cost back out. This is the same amortization principle that made caching beat trimming—applied backward, at the point where Zone B itself becomes the quadratic term.

**Untrained selector (bad proxy picks)**: The lexical/IDF scorer made destructive mistakes because it wasn't trained on the task. Fix: move selection into the summarizer. At the rare epoch when branches get collapsed anyway, ask the strong model: "Which of these 40 branches still bear on open work?"—far more reliable than cosine distance. Pin the active path unconditionally; everything else votes.

Combined, these three give you **hierarchical Zone B collapse**: old branches fold into super-summaries (the new tombstones), at budget-triggered epochs (the new cadence), chosen by LLM ranking (the new selector). DSA-on-branches isn't dead; it just needs a calendar and a demotion from per-turn to per-epoch.

**When to ship it**: not yet. At current scale (a handful of branches), Zone B never hits budget; the failure mode only matters at 100+ branches. v5.6 already wins without it. Ship the code when the conversation horizon makes Zone B budgets binding—not before, and with temperature pinned to a baseline, because 10-vs-37-turn trajectory variance will otherwise bury the measurement.
